correctness.rationale: Support maximization splits exactly into selecting root versus optimal subtrees. The positive increment e_(b,r)=E(W-sum child Y)_+ obeys e_(b,r)<=M rho^(b^r) by lower bounding every child optimum with its leaf antichain and exponential Markov. Series telescoping, branching coupling and strict r=1 increment yield all constants/rates. Gaussian radial factorization gives exact spherical mean width, Poincare bound Var(Y)<=b^h gives concentration, and per-node probability plus a union bound proves localization. Independent exhaustive antichain optimization matched support DP in 100 test instances; not a universal proof.

value.rationale: Mean width and random support localization are intrinsic metric/normal-fan statistics for natural exponentially large poset polytopes. The explicit superexponential finite-depth error and strict b-dependence form a nontrivial sharp asymptotic description beyond deterministic inradius or antichain counting.

final_claim: For fixed b>=2, signed antichain support satisfies Y_h=max(|G|,sum_b Y_(h-1)). Normalized constants c_(b,h)=b^-h E Y_h converge strictly to c_b with stated superexponential remainder, mu<c_(b+1)<c_b; spherical width divided by sqrt(n_h) tends to 2(b-1)c_b/b. All support vertices are within O(log log n_h) levels from leaves with high probability.
limitations: Fixed b and h→infinity; c_b defined recursively without elementary closed form; localization is an upper bound only.
